Log Workout
Today’s selected workout loads here automatically. Edit the exercise, sets, reps, or weight to match what you actually do; those edited values are saved to History and used for future recommendations.
How workout logging works
For strength work, log sets, reps, weight, effort, and technique. Exact RPE and individual-set timing are optional. For cardio, enter the activity’s actual duration and any useful distance, pace, power, or heart-rate data. The workout timer handles autosave and overall session time; the duration entered on the activity card is what counts toward cardio training. An active workout remains saved while you change tabs, open an exercise guide, background the app, or reload.

How Helio Influences Training
Actual workout performance stays the strongest signal.
Direct performance
Highest priority
What you completed, the reps and weight you used, effort, and technique guide future progression. Exact RPE is optional; if you enter it, also mark how sure you are.
Recovery metrics
Can scale training down
Unusual HRV, resting heart rate, sleep, BioCharge, or recent activity can hold a progression or make an optional workout easier.
Body fatigue
Muscle recovery
Feeling physically fatigued can reduce strength work. Consistently handling more work while feeling fresh can support a higher future target.
Energy / sleepiness
Alertness
Low energy is kept separate from muscle fatigue. It matters most for very hard cardio, explosive work, and technical training.
Soreness
Recovery caution
Soreness can make a workout more conservative without being treated as the same thing as sleepiness.
Good wearable day
Normal plan
Good wearable data and feeling fresh can remove unnecessary caution, but they do not trigger an aggressive jump in training.

Context / trend

Bodyweight Tracker
Log the number shown on the scale. Context helps the app compare it with earlier measurements.
Why weigh-in context matters
Time of day, food, fluids, bathroom timing, exercise, and clothing can move the scale. The app keeps the number you entered and gives less weight to measurements taken under very different conditions.
Time matters even if your stomach is empty; a bedtime weigh-in is not treated as equivalent to a standardized morning weigh-in.
Best comparison: morning, after the bathroom, before food, drinks, or exercise, with minimal clothing. Other weigh-ins still count; the app keeps the number you entered and treats it as a less direct comparison.
Add a measurement to establish your bodyweight timeline.

Equipment profile — change only when needed
Keep separate availability lists for your usual gym, home, and travel. The same equipment can be available in more than one location; changing one profile does not remove it from another. Automatic workouts use the active profile, while every exercise remains available for manual selection.
Adaptive weights: Same-exercise history is strongest. New/returning exercises use conservative evidence from related Barbell Strength, kettlebell, and gym movements.

Calisthenics Workout Builder
Build or edit a bodyweight workout for any date.
Want a starting point? Build from recent training, current recovery, upcoming anchors, and the equipment checked below.
1. Equipment
How equipment changes exercise selection
A high pull-up bar enables vertical pulls/hangs; a low-row setup enables inverted rows; dip bars enable parallel-bar dips; an ab wheel enables rollout progressions; and bands enable assisted/resisted band work. A pull-up bar alone does not imply a low-row setup.
2. Focus
3. Difficulty
4. Optimal Sets & Reps
Each movement has its own rep or hold range. The app first adds reps or time, then moves to a harder variation, greater range of motion, or more resistance after you master that range. Sources are available on every exercise card.
How Optimal progression works
Exact performance on the current variation is the strongest evidence. Related Barbell Strength, KB, Gym, class, and other calisthenics work can inform the starting target through the relationship model, but cannot substitute for direct skill-specific performance. The exact app window is an evidence-informed programming rule, not a claim that one study proved a uniquely optimal number. Every exercise card includes its supporting citations.
5. Time Available
Progression: direct performance on the same movement matters most. Related training can make a small difference when there is not enough direct history yet.

Adaptive LSS + Sprints Engine
There is no fixed 18-week conditioning rotation anymore. LSS / Aerobic and Sprints / HIC are modeled as separate families, then the specific session is generated from your schedule, workout history, recency, category balance, and recent recovery signals.
FactorHow the app uses it
LSS & Sprints / HIC Library
Easy LSS / Aerobic and harder Sprints / HIC are shown as separate training families. They still share the underlying saved conditioning session type so existing history and recommendation logic remain compatible.
Adaptive by default. Choosing a session here creates a one-day override for the selected conditioning date.
How recommendations are ranked
The engine considers recency, LSS / sprint balance, logged execution quality, recovery, equipment, local fatigue, future fixed sessions, and training priorities.
Program Settings
Current position and base training maxes. Adaptive block adjustments and manual overrides are managed in Barbell Strength Maxes.
Advanced program timeline controls
Use carefully. Changing Current Global Week re-anchors Week 1. It does not alter completed history.
Training priorities
Choose what the flexible days should emphasize. Your fixed Barbell Strength sessions stay fixed.
This only changes automatic suggestions. You can still choose Calisthenics at any time.
Running location changes suggestions, not your available choices. Enable home kettlebells if they can be used for a second workout away from the gym.
The pool default pre-fills new swim logs. One length means one trip from wall to wall. Enter completed lengths and the app calculates total distance and pace. Actual RPE, heart rate, pace, and your own response can override the usual light-swim assumption.

Trends & Data Dashboard
Detailed training, recovery, workload, and progression data. Nothing on this screen changes your plan by itself.

Weekly Training

Completed workouts and their estimated training effect by week.

Training Balance

Strength, speed, endurance, power, and work capacity compared with your recent training and performance.

LSS + Sprints Volume

Weekly LSS / Aerobic and Sprints / HIC volume are tracked separately.

Recovery — HRV

Daily HRV values with the recent rolling direction.

Recovery — Resting HR & Sleep

Resting heart rate and sleep hours over time.

Current Muscle Fatigue

Estimated from recent workouts, effort, completion quality, and time since each muscle was trained.

Work by Muscle

Estimated working sets by muscle. Compound exercises also give partial credit to supporting muscles.

Cardio Progress by Activity

Running, walking, cycling, swimming, rowing, and rucking improve separately based on the results you log.

Exercise Progress

Recent results, trend, plateaus, and how much history is available for each strength exercise.

Cardio Fitness

Aerobic fitness, sprint repeatability, work capacity, and power are tracked separately.

Recommendation Accuracy

Shows how closely workout difficulty matched the estimate and which recovery inputs have been useful for you.

Heart Rate & Thresholds

Personal heart-rate ranges based on your sustained workouts, with supporting VO₂ and heart-rate-recovery trends when available.

Critical Speed / Power

Running, cycling, and rowing estimates built only from hard efforts with enough usable data.

Cardio Intensity

Estimated easy, moderate, and hard minutes from your thresholds, heart rate, effort, and workout type. This is context, not a fixed quota.

Strength & Repeatability

Strength trend, bodyweight context, performance across sets, and actual rest when individual sets are logged.

Recovery Response / Days Off

Learns whether your next-session outcomes tend to be better after Full Rest, Active Recovery, and different spacing windows. Used only as a modest tie-breaker.

Heat & Environment

Heat, humidity, and elevation help explain why the same workout may feel different under different conditions.

Hybrid Progress — Weight, Strength, LSS & Sprints

Compares recent, mid-term, and long-term changes. Bodyweight provides context; performance remains the goal.

Recovery / Fueling Watch

Cautious multi-signal trend flag from bodyweight, performance and recovery. It is advisory only and never diagnoses a medical condition.

Consistency & Normal Variation

Shows whether a change is larger than your usual day-to-day variation and how well pace or power holds during longer workouts.

Strength Stimulus & Exercise Order

Separates strength, hypertrophy, power and fatigue stimulus while accounting for where an exercise occurred in the session and how much rest was required.

Sensor Quality

Shows how reliable the available heart-rate and wearable data appear to be.

Time of Day & Altitude

Compares your actual results by time of day and accounts for recent altitude exposure when data are available.

Personalization Checks

A personal adjustment stays off until it improves predictions on later workouts.

Fitness and Short-Term Fatigue

Longer-term progress and recent fatigue can move in different directions. A tired day does not necessarily mean fitness is falling.

Last 7 Days of Training Stress

Estimated stress across major movement and cardio categories. The window moves each day instead of resetting on Monday.

Weekly Volume Response

Estimates how much weekly work each muscle has handled well. Early estimates are shown with lower confidence.

If I Train Today

Compares workout options using current fatigue, recent training, goals, and upcoming fixed workouts.

Deload Check

Looks for several signs of accumulated fatigue before suggesting an easier stretch of training.

Recommendation Inputs

Shows the main goals, fatigue signals, and confidence levels affecting today’s recommendations.

This is a temporary bridge, not Base Building. It pauses six-week program numbering, keeps the next block intact, and uses adaptive gym, bodyweight, LSS / Aerobic, Sprints / HIC, and recovery sessions around the selected emphasis. BASE BUILDING
Build Strength-Endurance Circuit
Choose the equipment you expect to have most often. The app will keep one primary circuit for the full eight-week block and only substitute on individual days when necessary.
Equipment available
Kettlebell setup
Choose what is physically available for this session. The 40 lb BowFlex 840 uses its actual dial settings: 8, 12, 20, 25, 35, or 40 lb (3.5, 5.5, 9, 11, 16, or 18 kg). The 70 lb adjustable bells use 12–32 kg in 2 kg steps. Single-bell setups exclude double-kettlebell movements.
Today’s SE dose
Outside Base Building, each Strength-Endurance workout stands on its own. The app chooses 2–3 circuits and 15–50 reps from your available time, recent training, how you feel, and what is scheduled next.
Circuit preview
The primary circuit stays stable across Weeks 1–5. A one-day equipment change creates substitutions for that date only; the next SE day returns to the primary circuit.
